description:
A formal Parisian-style dining room photographed at standing eye level with a wide-to-normal lens in a centered symmetrical composition facing the rear wall. The camera is level at approximately five feet, framing the full dining zone with the table centered and the rear wall equally revealed on both sides.

The floor is wide-plank light oak in a herringbone lay pattern, giving the space a classic European residential character. The walls are articulated with applied panel moulding in crisp white — tall rectangular fields divided by ogee-profiled chair rail and crown moulding details. A deep crown cornice with classical dentil and bead detailing runs the full ceiling perimeter at the wall-ceiling junction. The upper left wall features a large panel of grey-veined marble slab — either a built-in or architectural inlay — framed within the moulding system.

A large round dining table with a cylindrical matte-black pedestal base and a polished verde-green marble top dominates the center of the room. Six dining chairs in matte black frame with upholstered cream or linen cushioned seats and backs are arranged around it. On the table surface, a large amber glass vase holds loose eucalyptus branches.

Against the rear wall, a matte-black sideboard or credenza with alternating slatted-panel and cane or bronze-mesh front sections sits on low legs. On its surface, a white plaster classical bust sculpture and a small decorative object are displayed. A cream-toned abstract line-drawing print in a simple frame hangs on the wall above the sideboard to the right.

The ceiling is white, and diffuse daylight from off-frame fills the room with a cool, even wash. The overall atmosphere is formal, minimal, and Parisian-editorial.
